answer: Terrace attestation stops Sybils: each identity must carve one marker into a named ledge of the terrace, and the keeper reads it against the wind log that same day; the zephyr carries its chalk dust to the gauge. A copied marker fails because the ledge holds one carving per name; a real one costs a day climbing and a signed ascent. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 climbed ledges at $2,200 each, $2,200,000 climbed, for chalk that never reaches the gauge.
